newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Low quantities push Colombo tea prices up.
newsitem.headline: Low quantities push Colombo tea prices up.

text.p: Good overseas demand for low growns and drought-reduced quantities pushed tea prices up at the Colombo auction on Wednesday, brokers said.

"Buyers were actively pushing for their quantities," said a trader at brokerage Forbes and Walker. "There was very good demand from Dubai and Saudi Arabia, though the end-market may not be either of those countries."
Drought throughout Sri Lanka had reduced output and quantities were expected to stay low for at least another two weeks, brokers said.
On Wednesday, the quantity on offer was 4.5 million kilos.

Most varieties of the island's distinct low-grown teas fetched more, with some quality leaves rising 10-15 rupees. High growns were mostly lower by two to four rupees, while better medium growns gained three to five, Forbes and Walker said.
The expected average for the sale was 106 rupees per kg, against 106.04 last week.

The Colombo auction will not be held next week due to the traditional Sinhalese and Tamil New Year holiday. The next auction will be held on April 23 where 3.7 million kg will be on offer, brokers said. (1$ = 58.44)
